shipped_rows.title_o: The Small Firm Effect and the Entrepreneurial Spawning of Scientists and Engineers

blind_target.authors: Gompers P, Lerner J, Scharfstein DS
blind_target.title: Entrepreneurial spawning: Public corporations and the genesis of new ventures, 1986 to 1999.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We begin by replicating prior results regarding firm size and the likelihood of becoming an entrepreneur (e.g., Elfenbein et al. 2010, Gompers et al. 2005, Kacperczyk 2012, Sørensen 2007).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Overall, we are able to replicate the commonly found “small-firm effect,” but when we restrict our analyses to observe workers in dissolved firms alone, we no longer find the negative effect.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors confirm the cited small-firm result in the ordinary sample and explicitly report its disappearance and reversal among defunct firms. Their aggregate statement distinguishes these outcomes.
